dependency_graph.assessment: Graph resolves pycompression/python-isal and shows Debian/Ubuntu resolute already builds python3-isal 1.8.0 for riscv64, dynamically linked against libisal2 2.31.1 (riscv64 exists) plus libc6 and python3. This agrees with riscv64 viability of the C extension. It does not model the wheel build graph: the checkout's build backend is setuptools with setuptools-scm >=9.2, the ISA-L git submodule statically built by make, nasm for x86 only; those edges are absent. Reverse dependencies (xopen, aiohttp-fast-zlib, asammdf) are present only for amd64/arm64 in the graph, which is an omission or genuine lag for riscv64, not evidence either way. Debian links libisal2 dynamically while the PyPI wheel bundles ISA-L statically (graph/wheel difference).

proposal.architecture_precedent: Shared-host topology: all Linux architectures run on ubuntu-latest, aarch64 is an include row in the build matrix (cibw_archs_linux aarch64, QEMU platforms arm64). Recommend adding a riscv64 include row with before_all 'true' and extending the QEMU condition and platforms to riscv64. Do not use ubuntu-24.04-riscv: upstream has no native-per-architecture runner rows and no documented incompatibility with QEMU (cibuildwheel supports manylinux/musllinux riscv64 images).
proposal.build_backend_native_dependencies: setuptools>=77 + setuptools-scm>=9.2 (custom build_ext in setup.py); statically builds the intel/isa-l git submodule (7c3479e, v2.32.1) with make -f Makefile.unx; nasm only on x86; no other native libs.
proposal.contribution_rules: README: make a PR or issue; PR template requires CHANGELOG.rst entry and docs; no CLA/DCO; develop is the PR base; maintainer favours small, well-tested diffs.
proposal.existing_riscv64_work: None in python-isal issues/PRs. ISA-L ships initial riscv64 support (2.32.0) and open RVV PRs/issues. Downstream: RISE build-isal.yml (PR 1047, 1.8.0) and Debian/Ubuntu/ALT riscv64 packages.
proposal.fork_guards: None in ci.yml (no github.repository conditions); only tag/branch conditions and environment 'pypi' trusted publishing.
proposal.rationale: A concrete, bounded configuration patch exists: add a riscv64 include row to the build_wheels matrix of .github/workflows/ci.yml following the aarch64 precedent (shared ubuntu-latest host plus QEMU via docker/setup-qemu-action, cibuildwheel CIBW_ARCHS_LINUX), extend the QEMU step condition/platforms, list riscv64 in the README platform markers like #268 did for arm64, and add a CHANGELOG entry. RISE's downstream build proved the unmodified sources build and pass upstream tests on riscv64 (PR 1047). No upstream objection to riscv64 exists, ISA-L 2.32.1 declares riscv64 support (portable C path via Makefile.unx). Risks: single maintainer sensitive to PR size, release complexity and untested wheels; QEMU build is slow (aarch64 takes 32 min) and gates the PyPI upload; the PR must be minimal.
proposal.release_coverage: PyPI isal 1.9.1 (2026-11-03/04): manylinux2014+2_28 x86_64 and aarch64, musllinux_1_2 x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, win_amd64, sdist; no riscv64.
proposal.release_graph: ci.yml on push of tags: lint/package-checks/test-static/test-dynamic/test-arch/test-sanitizers gate make_sdist and build_wheels (cibuildwheel: ubuntu x86_64, ubuntu aarch64 via QEMU, macOS x2, Windows); upload_to_pypi downloads cibw-* artifacts and publishes with trusted publishing (environment pypi, tags only, test PyPI for tags containing '-').
risks: QEMU riscv64 emulation is slower than aarch64 (32 min) and may time out or segfault like past aarch64 attempts (#158)

ci_history.findings: Wheels are built only on tags. Linux aarch64 uses a shared ubuntu-latest host with QEMU (architecture-list/matrix include row), not a native runner. riscv64 should follow: a matrix include row cibw_archs_linux riscv64 plus extending the QEMU step condition and platforms. nasm is x86-only so before_all can be 'true'. An aarch64 QEMU build takes about 32 minutes; riscv64 will be slower. Develop's red TSAN job is unrelated. There are no fork guards. Adding the row also adds the row to the needs-gated release, so a riscv64 build failure would block PyPI upload (the maintainer's #313 requirement that releases need all builds).

data.summary: python-isal (PyPI: isal, latest 1.9.1) ships wheels for x86_64/aarch64 manylinux and musllinux, macOS and Windows but no riscv64. Upstream has never discussed riscv64 (no issue or PR among all 337 issues/PRs). The wheels are built with cibuildwheel in .github/workflows/ci.yml; aarch64 is built on ubuntu-latest through QEMU as a matrix include row. A bounded patch following that precedent (a riscv64 include row, QEMU platform condition, README platform markers, changelog) is feasible; the bundled ISA-L 2.32.1 builds via Makefile.unx, which falls back to portable C for riscv64 (no RVV/Zbc assembly). Recommendation: develop, configuration_integration, keeping the diff small because the single maintainer rejects large PRs and is wary of release-process complexity and untested wheels.

summary: python-isal 1.9.1 has no riscv64 wheel and upstream has never discussed riscv64 (all 105 issues and 232 PRs checked). aarch64 precedent: ubuntu-latest + QEMU include row in ci.yml build_wheels. Recommend develop/configuration_integration: add riscv64 include row, QEMU platform condition, README markers, CHANGELOG entry. Bundled ISA-L 2.32.1 builds portable C on riscv64 via Makefile.unx (no RVV asm). Risks: single maintainer rejects large PRs, slow QEMU build gating releases. No ecosystem report exists.
